main_chase_cards.name: Dunsparce
main_chase_cards.why: Dunsparce is not loud in the way Charizard or Celebi are loud, which is exactly why this route matters. The card turns a strange, shy Johto tunnel creature into a store-distributed information object: a little free promo that says the TCG was not only expanding through packs and tournaments, but through paper handouts, local stores, and kids picking up news.

key_artists.name: Atsuko Nishida
key_artists.why: Nishida's presence makes this tiny insert feel much bigger. She is tied to the franchise's cutest and most emotionally durable design language, including Pikachu and much of the Eevee family; on Dunsparce, that same eye for softness makes an oddball land snake feel collectible rather than disposable.

claims.text: The local catalog, Bulbapedia, and PokeBoon align on January 1, 2001 for Pokemon Card Information Vol. 1 / ポケモンカードインフォメーション その1 Dunsparce distribution.
Bulbapedia states the Dunsparce promo was available in Japan in the first volume of Pokemon Card Information and distributed for free at participating stores from January 1, 2001.
The local release family models one row: Dunsparce source index 221, with the promotion note Pokemon Card Information Vol. 1 insert.
Bulbapedia's 2001 unnumbered-promo table places Dunsparce before Neo Spring Road prizes and before later Pokemon Card Information Vol. 2 Bellossom and Vol. 3 Pryce's Lapras rows.

Pokemon Card Information Vol. 1 is a useful route because it shows the TCG distributing memory through free information handouts, not only through booster products, tournaments, CDs, books, or manga volumes.

Atsuko Nishida / 西田敦子 is documented by Bulbapedia as a long-running Pokemon franchise artist and designer, including work tied to Pikachu, Eevee/Eeveelutions, games, animation concepts, and many TCG illustrations.

narrative.human_title: Pokemon Card Information Vol. 1 — Dunsparce as store-counter memory
narrative.why_it_matters: This is a humble object, and that is the charm. Pokemon Card Information Vol. 1 does not feel like a grand prize or a cinematic Premium File; it feels like a kid finding a free information packet at a participating shop and discovering that even Dunsparce, the shy land snake that vanishes into holes, has a place in the TCG's paper ecosystem. The route tells us how Pokemon kept assembling itself in public: through magazines, books, tournaments, store counters, and little inserts that made ordinary Pokemon feel worth saving.

claims.text: The local catalog anchors Dunsparce as source index 221 in the Pokemon Card Information Vol. 1 unnumbered-promo source row.
Bulbapedia identifies the card as Dunsparce LV.14 / ノコッチ Nokocchi, a Colorless-type Basic Pokemon card with HP 40.
Bulbapedia lists Paralyzing Gaze / にらむ and Drill Tail / ドリルしっぽ as the card's attacks, with Fighting weakness, Psychic resistance, and one retreat cost.
Bulbapedia, PokeBoon, and Pokumon identify Atsuko Nishida / 西田敦子 as the illustrator for the Dunsparce Information Pack promo.
Bulbapedia records the bottom-border text as Information Pack bonus card part 1, making the route itself a visible card-detail clue.
Bulbapedia states the card's Pokedex entry comes from Pokemon Silver; on the card, the entry describes Dunsparce fleeing by digging with its tail when seen and floating slightly with its wings.

Atsuko Nishida's broader Pokemon role includes Pikachu, Eevee/Eeveelutions, early games, animation concepts, and many TCG illustrations, which makes this small Dunsparce row part of a much larger visual lineage.

Dunsparce matters here because the card is almost anti-chase: quiet, non-holo, store-distributed, and full of route clues. That makes it ideal for an agentic catalog that values how Pokemon was assembled, not only which names dominate the market.

narrative.human_title: Dunsparce — source index 221, the quiet shop-counter oddball
narrative.why_it_matters: Dunsparce is the opposite of a market thunderclap, and that is why this card earns a real note. Atsuko Nishida, one of the hands behind Pikachu's softness and the Eevee family's emotional gravity, draws this strange little land snake for a free store information packet. The result is wonderfully modest: Paralyzing Gaze, Drill Tail, a Silver-era Pokedex line about vanishing underground, and a border that tells you exactly which paper route carried it into the world.
